subject: Strength of Materials
summary: torsion of solid and hollow shafts, power transmission, compound shafts, thin cylindrical and spherical shells, and close-coiled helical springs

questions.text: The polar section modulus Z<sub>p</sub> of a hollow circular shaft of outer diameter D<sub>o</sub> and inner diameter D<sub>i</sub> is
solution: Concept: Zp = J / rmax, where rmax is the outer radius, because the shear stress is greatest at the outer surface.
J = π(D<sub>o</sub><sup>4</sup> − D<sub>i</sub><sup>4</sup>)/32 and r<sub>max</sub> = D<sub>o</sub>/2
Zp = J/(Do/2) = π(Do4 − Di4)/(16 Do), so T = τmax Zp.

Exam tip: Option (C) is the classic trap: the section modulus of a hollow shaft is NOT the difference of the solid moduli (πDo3/16 − πDi3/16), because both parts must be referred to the same outer radius.

questions.text: A solid shaft of 60 mm diameter runs at 180 rpm. If the maximum shear stress is limited to 50 MPa, the power it can transmit (in kW) is ______
solution: Concept: Torque capacity from the torsion formula, then P = 2πNT/60.
Exam tip: Keep units straight: T in N·m and N in rpm give P in watts. A slip with N·mm makes the answer 1000 times too large.

questions.text: A solid steel shaft must transmit 75 kW at 300 rpm. The shear stress must not exceed 60 MPa and the angle of twist must not exceed 0.25° per metre length (G = 80 GPa). The minimum shaft diameter (in mm) is ______
solution: Concept: Design for strength and for stiffness separately; the larger diameter satisfies both.
d4 = 32J/π → d = 91.4 mm. Stiffness governs.
Exam tip: Long transmission shafts are usually stiffness-limited. Always convert the twist limit to radians per mm before using T/J = Gθ/L.

questions.text: The stepped steel shaft ABC shown is fixed at A. AB is 50 mm in diameter and 1.0 m long; BC is 30 mm in diameter and 0.5 m long. Torques of 1.5 kN·m at B and 0.5 kN·m at C act in the same sense. The maximum shear stress in the shaft is
solution: Concept: Shafts in series: find the internal torque in each segment from the part to the right of a cut, then apply τ = 16T/(πd3) segment by segment.
Segment BC: TBC = 0.5 kN·m → τ = 16 × 0.5 × 106/(π × 303) = 94.3 MPa
Segment AB: T<sub>AB</sub> = 1.5 + 0.5 = 2.0 kN·m → τ = 16 × 2 × 10<sup>6</sup>/(π × 50<sup>3</sup>) = 81.5 MPa
So the thin segment BC governs: τmax = 94.3 MPa. (With G = 80 GPa, the twist at C is θAB + θBC = 0.0407 + 0.0393 = 0.0800 rad = 4.59°.)
Exam tip: The largest torque does not always give the largest stress. Compare T/d3 for each segment.

questions.text: A composite shaft is made of a solid steel core of 40 mm diameter rigidly bonded inside a brass tube of 60 mm outer diameter, as shown. The shaft carries a torque of 2 kN·m. With G<sub>steel</sub> = 80 GPa and G<sub>brass</sub> = 40 GPa, the maximum shear stress in the brass (in MPa) is ______
solution: Concept: Shafts in parallel (statically indeterminate): both parts twist through the same angle, so torque divides in proportion to the torsional rigidity GJ.
J<sub>s</sub> = π × 40<sup>4</sup>/32 = 2.513 × 10<sup>5</sup> mm<sup>4</sup>; J<sub>b</sub> = π(60<sup>4</sup> − 40<sup>4</sup>)/32 = 1.021 × 10<sup>6</sup> mm<sup>4</sup>
G<sub>s</sub>J<sub>s</sub> = 2.011 × 10<sup>10</sup>, G<sub>b</sub>J<sub>b</sub> = 4.084 × 10<sup>10</sup> N·mm<sup>2</sup> → T<sub>b</sub> = 2 × 4.084/6.095 = 1.340 kN·m, T<sub>s</sub> = 0.660 kN·m
Exam tip: Shear strain is continuous across the bond, but shear stress jumps at the interface by the ratio Gs/Gb (here 52.5 → 26.3 MPa).

questions.text: A shaft section carries a bending moment of 2 kN·m and a torque of 1.5 kN·m. The equivalent bending moment (maximum principal stress theory) is
solution: Concept: Combined bending and torsion: Me = [M + √(M2 + T2)]/2 and Te = √(M2 + T2).
T<sub>e</sub> = √(2<sup>2</sup> + 1.5<sup>2</sup>) = 2.5 kN·m
Exam tip: 2.50 kN·m is Te, which goes with the maximum shear stress theory. This topic returns in detail with shaft design.

questions.text: The surface of a solid 80 mm diameter shaft running at 500 rpm carries a strain gauge inclined at 45° to the shaft axis, as shown. Under steady torque the gauge reads a tensile strain of 200 × 10<sup>−6</sup>. With G = 80 GPa, the power transmitted (in kW) is ______
solution: Concept: In pure torsion the surface element is in pure shear, so the principal strains at ±45° are ±γ/2.
Exam tip: Using γ = ε45 (forgetting the factor 2) halves the answer to 84.2 kW, a favourite distractor.

questions.text: A thin cylinder of internal diameter 1 m and wall thickness 12 mm carries an internal pressure of 1.5 MPa (E = 200 GPa, ν = 0.3). The increase in its diameter is
solution: Concept: The hoop strain controls the diameter change: εh = (σh − νσl)/E, with σh = pd/2t and σl = pd/4t.
Exam tip: 0.313 mm ignores the Poisson effect of the longitudinal stress. In compact form, Δd = (pd2/4tE)(2 − ν).

questions.text: A thin spherical shell of 1.2 m internal diameter and 8 mm wall thickness is subjected to an internal pressure of 1.6 MPa (E = 200 GPa, ν = 0.3). The increase in its internal volume (in cm<sup>3</sup>) is ______
solution: Concept: In a thin sphere the wall stress pd/4t acts equally in all directions, so εv = 3ε = 3(σ/E)(1 − ν).
Exam tip: 1 m3 = 106 cm3 = 1000 litres. Unit conversion is where most wrong answers in this question come from.

questions.text: A thin cylindrical air receiver of 2 m diameter is made of 20 mm plate. The allowable tensile stress is 120 MPa, the longitudinal joint efficiency is 80 % and the circumferential joint efficiency is 50 %. The maximum safe internal pressure is
solution: Concept: The hoop stress is resisted by the longitudinal joint, the longitudinal stress by the circumferential joint. Check both and take the smaller pressure.
Longitudinal: pd/(4t) ≤ σ η<sub>c</sub> → p = 4 × 20 × 120 × 0.5/2000 = 2.40 MPa
Safe pressure = smaller value = 1.92 MPa
Exam tip: Matching the joint with the stress it carries is the whole question: longitudinal joint ↔ hoop stress, circumferential joint ↔ longitudinal stress.

questions.text: A strain gauge fixed circumferentially on a closed thin cylinder (internal diameter 600 mm, wall thickness 6 mm) reads a hoop strain of 250 × 10<sup>−6</sup> when the cylinder is pressurised. With E = 200 GPa and ν = 0.3, the internal pressure (in MPa) is ______
solution: Concept: εh = (σh − νσl)/E = (pd/4tE)(2 − ν).
Exam tip: Ignoring Poisson's ratio would give 1.00 MPa; the longitudinal stress reduces the hoop strain, so the true pressure is higher.

questions.text: The spring system shown carries a load of 250 N. Spring 1 (k<sub>1</sub> = 10 N/mm) is connected in series with springs 2 (k<sub>2</sub> = 20 N/mm) and 3 (k<sub>3</sub> = 30 N/mm), which act in parallel. The deflection of the load is
solution: Concept: Parallel springs share the deflection (stiffnesses add); series springs share the load (flexibilities add).
Parallel pair: k<sub>23</sub> = 20 + 30 = 50 N/mm
Series with k<sub>1</sub>: 1/k = 1/10 + 1/50 → k = 8.33 N/mm
δ = 250/8.33 = 30.0 mm (= 25 mm in spring 1 + 5 mm in the parallel pair)
Exam tip: 45.8 mm treats all three in series and 4.2 mm all three in parallel. Read the connection from the figure before writing any formula.

questions.text: A close-coiled helical spring of 10 mm wire and 60 mm mean coil diameter (G = 80 GPa) must deflect 25 mm under an axial load of 800 N. The number of active turns required (whole number) is ______
solution: Concept: δ = 8WD3n/(Gd4), so n = Gd4δ/(8WD3).
Turns must be whole numbers, so provide 15 active turns.
Exam tip: Rounding the turns up makes the spring slightly softer (more deflection), which is usually the safe side for a deflection requirement; stress is unaffected by n.

questions.text: The Wahl correction factor for a close-coiled helical spring with a spring index of 6 is closest to
solution: Concept: KW = (4C − 1)/(4C − 4) + 0.615/C combines the curvature and direct-shear corrections.
Exam tip: 1.083 is the direct-shear factor alone (1 + 0.5/C) and 1.150 is only the first term. A smaller index C means a larger correction.

questions.text: A close-coiled helical spring of stiffness k is cut into three equal lengths, and the three pieces are placed side by side in parallel to carry a load. The stiffness of the arrangement is
solution: Concept: k = Gd4/(8D3n) ∝ 1/n. Each piece has n/3 turns, so each piece has stiffness 3k.
Three pieces in parallel: keq = 3k + 3k + 3k = 9k
Exam tip: The same rule holds for any spring or elastic bar: stiffness is inversely proportional to the active length.
